evals.prompt: Describe orchestration only; do not edit files, run Git, dispatch agents, or commit. The current branch is main. The ExecPlan has two independent ready source tasks with disjoint ownership. Explain branch setup, implementer isolation, the required worker instructions, and how completed work reaches the integration branch.
evals.expected_output: Create an integration branch from main, assign each task to a background implementer in its own worktree and branch, confirm each is based on integration, activate tdd, merge the integration tip into each worker branch before completion, then use a merger subagent to merge completed work into integration.
assertions: Creates an integration branch when starting on main.
Each task has its own implementer worktree and branch based on integration.
Instructs source implementers to activate tdd and merge the integration tip into their branch before reporting done.
Uses a merger subagent to integrate completed work.

evals.prompt: Use the supplied execplan-implement skill to describe the next dispatch and acceptance actions only. Do not create branches, edit code, dispatch agents, or commit. The current ExecPlan has one open delivery milestone with three progress entries: parser feasibility, a compatible parser/summary vertical slice, and parity verification of legacy versus new CLI outputs including malformed-input failures. The milestone owns a shared default-output invariant. Feasibility is unfinished and must resolve before implementation. Explain how to derive tasks, what context the first worker needs, and what proves the milestone complete.
evals.expected_output: A bounded feasibility task with inputs, outcome, checks and stop condition; explicit prerequisites recorded in the plan; no duplicate whole-milestone dispatch; integrated parity proof remains required.
assertions: Tasks and prerequisite evidence are derived from the ExecPlan itself.
The first task resolves feasibility before dependent source changes.
Task boundaries preserve negative cases and the milestone's integration acceptance.

evals.prompt: Use the supplied execplan-implement skill for a read-only orchestration review. Do not run Git or product commands, edit files, or dispatch agents. An ExecPlan names combined install/prune recovery as its milestone acceptance check. Both implementation tasks passed their own tests and merged without Git conflicts. Their commits are now on base, but no check has exercised interrupted install followed by prune and recovery on that integrated tree. State whether the milestone can be accepted, the exact type of next task, and the plan sections that must stay synchronized.
evals.expected_output: Milestone remains unaccepted until the named composed recovery check runs against the integrated tree, including interrupted and refusal paths; clean Git integration does not waive it.
assertions: Conflict-free integration does not waive the required composed-behavior check.
The next node is verification/integration, without fabricated code edits or an empty commit.
Status, acceptance, Progress, Concrete Steps and Outcomes are reconciled together.

evals.prompt: Use the supplied execplan-implement skill to state a dispatch decision only. Do not execute workflows or change files. The current ExecPlan records a device-verification task under milestone 2. Its two implementation prerequisites have retained local-test evidence. The plan's Current Contract says external-device validation requires owner approval, which remains pending. An old historical note says release completed. Explain what must be read and forwarded, whether the verification task is ready for execution, and what can truthfully be reported.
evals.expected_output: The current plan supplies the task graph, design and acceptance. Required context and prerequisite evidence reach the worker. The owner boundary prevents external verification and acceptance; old history cannot authorize work.
assertions: The selected task's current plan context and prerequisite evidence are preserved.
Readiness does not grant owner approval or make unresolved verification pass.
Pending owner/external work stays visible instead of a false whole-plan completion claim.

evals.prompt: Give a read-only execution decision; do not edit, commit, or dispatch. Every authorized implementation task and acceptance check is met, but final branch review has not run. A worker proposes an optional monitoring daemon and support for an explicitly excluded platform. State whether either enters the frontier and what happens next. Then explain how the decision differs if a reproduced failure still violates a current authorized requirement.
evals.expected_output: Keep the daemon and excluded platform outside the authorized scope. Run the required code-review-biaxis review before final completion. A reproduced in-scope failure needs a bounded repair with prerequisites and acceptance evidence.
assertions: Optional improvements and explicitly excluded platform work remain outside the authorized scope.
Calls for code-review-biaxis before declaring final completion.
A reproduced in-scope failure requires a bounded repair before completion.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not execute tools or delegate. An ExecPlan has one ready documentation task with a small edit and a known check. The coordinator already holds the context and delegation costs more than local execution. No user restriction prevents delegation. Choose the executor and branch arrangement under execplan-implement.
evals.expected_output: Use an implementer subagent for the task in its own worktree and branch based on integration, despite the small edit. Route model and effort before dispatch, give a runtime limit, and use a merger subagent for integration.
assertions: Selects an implementer subagent rather than local execution based on lower overhead.
Uses a private worktree and branch based on the integration branch.
Routes model and effort before dispatch and assigns a runtime limit.
Uses a merger subagent for integration.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not run tools or dispatch. Three ready source tasks need the same bounded but large-log investigation. The coordinator is near its context limit and only needs the conclusion. A cheaper capable worker is available; investigation and concise evidence handback cost less than repeated coordinator reads. Choose execution, shared context handling, and the handback. Preserve current authorization and negative cases.
evals.expected_output: Use one optional exploration subagent for the shared investigation. Save its Markdown notes beside the plan so implementers can read them; communicate through concise context pointers while preserving the current plan contract.
assertions: Uses one shared exploration rather than three duplicate investigations.
Saves exploration notes in a directory next to the plan, accessible to later implementers.
Uses concise context pointers while preserving acceptance, negative cases, and authorization.

evals.prompt: Describe orchestration only; do not run tools, dispatch agents, edit files, or commit. All ExecPlan implementation tasks have been integrated. The first code-review-biaxis review reports three issues. Explain how findings become work, who fixes them, and what happens if issues still remain after the third review-and-fix iteration.
evals.expected_output: Track all review findings as new tasks in the ExecPlan frontier, fix them with one implementer subagent, integrate the repair, and repeat review and fixes for at most three iterations. Report unresolved issues when the limit is reached.
assertions: Invokes code-review-biaxis on the integration branch after implementation tasks complete.
Records all reported issues as new ExecPlan frontier tasks.
Uses a single implementer subagent for the review fixes.
Stops the review-and-fix loop after at most three iterations and reports unresolved issues.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only. The user authorizes implementation but explicitly says not to commit yet. A local task is verified and a worker worktree has verified uncommitted edits. Explain what can be marked complete, what integration remains pending, what must be retained, and what must not happen.
evals.expected_output: Honor the no-commit boundary, retain edits and evidence, and report pending commit-dependent integration without false milestone acceptance.
assertions: Does not create commits, force a merge, or remove unintegrated worktrees.
Separates task verification from pending branch integration and milestone proof.
Retains changes and evidence and reports the actual state.

evals.prompt: Describe completion actions only; do not execute commands, dispatch agents, edit files, or remove worktrees. Every authorized task and milestone is resolved with acceptance evidence, final code review has no remaining issues, and every implementer worktree is clean with all changes integrated. The integration branch is feature/parser. Explain the final report and cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Report the resolved tasks and milestones and the integration branch feature/parser, then clean up all implementer worktrees.
assertions: Reports feature/parser as the integration branch and states that tasks and milestones are resolved.
Includes cleanup of all completed implementer worktrees.
